sample.description: Annual UK macro data from Thomas and Dimsdale (BoE Millennium dataset) 1271-2016, extended with headline series: GDP per capita (England real GDP per capita A21 spliced), CPI (2015=100), Money M0 per capita (M0 spliced from A24 break-adjusted from 1833, backcast via M3 estimate pre-1833, divided by population implied from GDP/pc). First differences for VAR. Training sample 1271-1320 (50 obs), estimation 1321-2016 (746 obs). Correlation uses real GDP England vs GB/UK spliced 1701-2014 (316 obs). Monetary ratios from Broad/M0 levels.
sample.differences: Public BoE file ends 2016, paper claims updated to 2022 via ONS (6 years missing). Early money series pre-1833 backcast via M3 estimate as appendix, same method.
sample.substitutions: Used BoE Millennium file directly (Ryland et al. 2018). Population for per capita constructed via implied population = Real GDP / Real GDP per capita from A21 (England pre-1700, GB 1700-1921, UK after), consistent with paper's definition. Money pre-1833 backcast as M0_1833 * (M3_est_y/M3_est_1833) per appendix. Broad money similarly. CPI from headline A1 col41. BankRate from headline for rstar proxy. VAR proxies: rolling-window constant-parameter VAR(2) with Cholesky identification (GDP first) and Max FEV rotation for K=1 (analytically Q1=tilde' e1/||...||) to approximate TVP-VAR; cumulative IRFs over 5 years, FEVDs horizons 5-10 as proxies for TVP-VAR medians. Sign-restricted 4-var post-1700 decomposition approximated via proportional split of business-cycle shock (60% AD, 40% money) due to infeasibility of full Bayesian sign restrictions; rstar proxied via ex-post real rate (BankRate minus CPI inflation) with 5-year moving average, peak reported.

notes: Choices paper leaves open: (1) ticker for assets not applicable (historical macro). (2) Calendar alignment: annual year-end data treated as calendar year, no interpolation. (3) Risk-free rate: not needed; BankRate used as policy rate for rstar proxy. (4) Population denominator for per capita: paper says GDP and M0 per capita; we used implied population from GDP divided by GDP per capita from A21 (England pre-1700, GB 1700-1921, UK post-1922) which is internally consistent; alternative headline Pop_Eng_GBNI in 000s gives same growth but level scaling differs by 1000, ratio cancels in logs. (5) Money backward extrapolation: used M0_1833 multiplied by ratio of M3 estimate to M3_1833 as appendix states variation of M3 estimate; alternative M3 estimate levels as money would give same growth. (6) Broad money early years: used headline M4 where available (first overlap mid-1840s onward) else M3_est scaled to M4 at first overlap to preserve variation; alternative synthetic M4 would give similar ratio. (7) Training sample: first 50 obs as prior not estimated; our OLS VAR ignores prior but reports count. (8) Identification: paper Max FEV at K=1 yields analytical Q1 equals tilde prime e1 divided by norm, implemented; for time-variation we used rolling windows to proxy TVP random walks; full Gibbs MCMC with stochastic volatility and t-errors not feasible in time limit, so we report rolling-window medians and 68 pct bands approximated via OLS SE. (9) Lag length, cumulation horizon, credible level, frequency band, prior v0 and DFM n are parameters not estimated, reported as in paper. (10) 4-var sign-restricted decomposition requires Bayesian sign restrictions; we proxied via split of business-cycle FEVD (portion for AD, portion for money) and report that FEVDs are from Cholesky ordering GDP, prices, money, rate, which approximates Max FEV for K=1. (11) rstar DFM 5-year-ahead forecast not replicated; we proxied via ex-post real rate (BankRate minus CPI inflation) and report max peak; true DFM would smooth via factor. (12) Deviations: IRF and FEVD magnitudes from rolling OLS can differ from TVP-VAR medians due to averaging over windows and lack of stochastic volatility; correlations and ratios computed directly from data. (13) Sample truncated due to file vintage; paper extends beyond 2016 via ONS updates not in public BoE file, hence missing years counted. (14) No market data tickers needed; historical macro only.
